evidence.quote: A personal access token (PAT) is the quickest and simplest way to authenticate in the API.
OAuth is an open-standard authentication protocol that allows you to approve one application interacting with another on your behalf without providing your username and password.
Treat your PAT like you would treat a password. Do not share it and do not display it online.

result.notes: Asana's REST API (developers.asana.com) supports OAuth 2.0 for multi-user apps and Personal Access Tokens (used as Bearer tokens) for scripts/single-user use, both self-serve from the Asana web app with no approval process found in docs. A free Asana account is sufficient to generate a PAT via the developer console (app.asana.com/0/my-apps); paid tiers only affect feature availability (e.g., Portfolios) and rate limits (150 req/min free vs 1500 paid per community sources), not baseline API access. Also supports Service Accounts (Enterprise-only, super-admin created) and OpenID Connect for user login, not counted as core API auth methods. No official Asana-published MCP server was found; multiple community MCP servers exist (e.g. roychri/mcp-server-asana, 148 stars). API surface is REST, ~167 endpoints per the apis.guru OpenAPI spec.
result.one_liner: Asana is a work/project management platform with a REST API for managing tasks, projects, portfolios, and workflows.
